verses: For the choirmaster, to be accompanied by flutes. A Psalm of David. Give ear to my words, O LORD; consider my groaning.
Attend to the sound of my cry, my King and my God, for to You I pray.
In the morning, O LORD, You hear my voice; at daybreak I lay my plea before You and wait in expectation.
For You are not a God who delights in wickedness; no evil can dwell with You.
The boastful cannot stand in Your presence; You hate all workers of iniquity.
You destroy those who tell lies; the LORD abhors the man of bloodshed and deceit.
But I will enter Your house by the abundance of Your loving devotion; in reverence I will bow down toward Your holy temple.
Lead me, O LORD, in Your righteousness because of my enemies; make straight Your way before me.
For not a word they speak can be trusted; destruction lies within them. Their throats are open graves; their tongues practice deceit.
Declare them guilty, O God; let them fall by their own devices. Drive them out for their many transgressions, for they have rebelled against You.
But let all who take refuge in You rejoice; let them ever shout for joy. May You shelter them, that those who love Your name may rejoice in You.
For surely You, O LORD, bless the righteous; You surround them with the shield of Your favor.
title: Wait in Expectation
season_line: Last week David prayed himself to sleep in Psalm 4; this morning, in Psalm 5, he wakes up and prays first thing, right where you are now.
big_idea: Morning prayer isn't a box to check. It's laying your day before God, then watching all day for His answer.
frame: Most mornings we hand God a quick list and walk off. David lays his requests out like an offering, then stays on the lookout. Walking with God today means praying, then actually expecting Him to show up in meetings, errands, and conversations, and noticing when He does. We don't get that access by being good enough. We come in only through the abundance of His loving devotion, a door Jesus opened wide ({{Hebrews 10:19-22|Hebrews 10:19–22}}). With Advent starting tomorrow, a season of watching and waiting, today is a fitting day to practice the posture: pray, then look up.

carry.text: In the morning, O LORD, You hear my voice; at daybreak I lay my plea before You and wait in expectation.

glance.head: A Morning Cry
glance.line: David asks God to hear his words and groans, laying his plea before Him at daybreak and waiting.

glance.head: A Holy God
glance.line: God takes no pleasure in evil; the boastful, the liars, and the violent cannot stand before Him.

glance.head: Entering by Mercy
glance.line: David comes into God's house only by His great love, and asks God to lead him straight.

glance.head: Words That Kill
glance.line: His enemies' mouths are full of deceit, and he asks God to judge their rebellion.

understand: Psalm 4 ended with David lying down in peace. Psalm 5 picks up at sunrise. The pair gives us a rhythm for walking with God: hand Him the night, hand Him the morning. David calls God my King and my God. This king of Israel knows he answers to a greater King.

Verses 4-6 can feel harsh, but they explain something good. God is holy, so evil can't settle in His presence. That's exactly why verse 7 begins with But. David doesn't get in because he's better than the liars. He enters by the abundance of Your loving devotion. That's God's covenant love, His loyal, never-quitting kindness ({{Exodus 34:6-7|Exodus 34:6–7}}).

Notice how much of this psalm is about speech: lies, deceit, tongues, throats like open graves. Paul quotes verse 9 in {{Romans 3:10-18|Romans 3:10–18}} to show that every human heart, not just David's enemies, needs rescue. The only one who could truly enter God's house on His own merit is Jesus, and He opens it to us.
The psalm ends wide open: let all who take refuge in You rejoice. The shield in verse 12 is the large kind that covered a soldier's whole body. God's favor doesn't just guard one side. It surrounds.

word.gloss: A Hebrew word for watching like a sentry on a wall, scanning the horizon for what's coming. It's the word Habakkuk uses when he stands at his post to see how God will answer ({{Habakkuk 2:1}}).

glow: by the abundance of Your loving devotion

god.short: Lay one specific request before God now, then watch for His answer today.
god.full: Before the day takes over, name one specific thing you're laying before God, out loud if you can. Set a midday reminder that just says 'Watching,' and pause to ask where He's at work in it.
god.why: David prays at daybreak and then keeps watch, like a sentry waiting for news ({{Psalm 5:3|Psalm 5:3}}).

together.short: Each name one thing you're laying before God, then pray 'Lead me' together.
together.full: Tell each other in one sentence what you're bringing to God today. Then pray verse 8 over each other: 'Lead them, O LORD; make Your way straight before them.'

others.short: Text a friend who's surrounded by pressure: you're praying God shields them today.
others.full: Think of a friend or coworker dealing with someone harsh or dishonest right now. Send a short text saying you prayed this morning that God would surround them like a shield.
others.why: God surrounds those who take refuge in Him with the shield of His favor ({{Psalm 5:11-12|Psalm 5:11–12}}).

tonight: What did each of us bring to God this morning, and where did we see Him answer, or where might we have missed it?

more.line: His mercies are new every morning; wait for Him.
Paul uses Psalm 5 to show everyone needs grace.
Jesus opens the way into God's house.
